(3) LAYER UP/DOWN + CONSEQUENCE: `grep -ran "process.on('SIG"` over apps/cli/src, packages/server/src, packages/server-core/src, packages/pi-agent-server/src and packages/shared/src finds exactly two registration sites in source — the CLI pair above, and packages/server/src/index.ts:376-377, which is the separate long-lived `nessy-server` daemon whose `shutdown` exits 0 for both signals (a different subsystem, correctly not the one cited). correctedState: apps/cli/src/index.ts:796-804 registers a single `onSignal` handler for both `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` inside `cmdRun` (our print-mode/non-interactive surface, `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` at :782); it cancels the session, runs `cleanup()`, and ends in `process.exit(130)` at :801. Because a registered handler suppresses Node's default SIGTERM disposition, a SIGTERM'd headless run exits 130 instead of the documented 143 — verified by control: the same script without the handlers exits 143. SIGINT correctly exits 130. The only other signal handlers in source are packages/server/src/index.ts:376-377 on the separate `nessy-server` daemon, which exits 0 for both. Fixing this means branching `onSignal` on the received signal name (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM) and updating the exit-code table at docs/cli.md:133.
